nl: In billing/pricing.py, introduce a module-level constant BLOCK_SIZE = 1024 after the module docstring (one blank line before it, two blank lines after it) and use it in place of the number 1024 in the three calculations. The string "1024.0" in version() stays unchanged.
oracle_program:
edit "billing/pricing.py" changes: [{insert: "BLOCK_SIZE = 1024\n", line: 3, position: before}]
search /\b1024\b(?!\.0")/ "billing/pricing.py" |> replace "BLOCK_SIZE"
reference_bash:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import os, pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('billing/pricing.py'); t = p.read_bytes().decode()
assert t.count('"""Pricing helpers."""\n\n') == 1, 'billing/pricing.py'
p.write_bytes(t.replace('"""Pricing helpers."""\n\n', '"""Pricing helpers."""\n\nBLOCK_SIZE = 1024\n\n').encode())
p = pathlib.Path('billing/pricing.py'); t = p.read_bytes().decode()
assert t.count('(1 + 1024)') == 1, 'billing/pricing.py'
p.write_bytes(t.replace('(1 + 1024)', '(1 + BLOCK_SIZE)').encode())
p = pathlib.Path('billing/pricing.py'); t = p.read_bytes().decode()
assert t.count('net * 1024\n') == 1, 'billing/pricing.py'
p.write_bytes(t.replace('net * 1024\n', 'net * BLOCK_SIZE\n').encode())
p = pathlib.Path('billing/pricing.py'); t = p.read_bytes().decode()
assert t.count('{net * 1024:.2f}') == 1, 'billing/pricing.py'
p.write_bytes(t.replace('{net * 1024:.2f}', '{net * BLOCK_SIZE:.2f}').encode())
EOF
